results.title: Zimbabwean author cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story

results.title: Ukraine: Dashcam captures massive explosion on Lviv street
results.content: A dashcam captured the moment a Russian projectile struck a building directly ahead of a car in Lviv, forcing the driver to reverse. The attack killed two people and injured at least 10 others.

results.title: Cameroon U17s fall to Venezuela in World Cup opener
results.content: Cameroon’s U17 team began their FIFA U17 World Cup campaign in Doha with a 2-1 defeat to Venezuela, leaving the players and coach Thomas Libiih looking to regroup ahead of their next Group K match.

results.title: Tanzania rally from two goals down to draw with Costa Rica in U17 World Cup debut
results.content: Tanzania’s U17 side fought back from two goals down to draw 2-2 with Costa Rica in their FIFA U17 World Cup debut in Doha.

results.content: The contemporary African art exhibition's official selection brings together 54 artists from 17 African countries, and runs until 19 December.

results.title: English captain and Bayern Munich star out of action after ankle injury

results.title: Strait of Hormuz: Athlete swims through war zone to expose war's environmental toll
results.content: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh completed a 15-kilometre swim through the Strait of Hormuz over three days in November 2026, braving explosions and burning tankers nearby. His three-day challenge aimed to expose the environmental damage caused by the war with Iran.

results.title: South Africa's former vice president and UN official dies aged 71

results.title: Japan: Autonomous air taxi completes passenger flight without a pilot
results.content: A pilotless electric flying taxi has carried a passenger during a demonstration, on Friday 20 November 2026, in Japan's Yamanashi Prefecture. The Chinese-built aircraft took off vertically and flew autonomously, offering a glimpse of a possible future for urban transport.

results.title: Haiti reaches deal with El Salvador to build three new prisons
results.content: The justice minister has not said how the prisons, to be constructed in collaboration with Haitian firms, wil be financed.

results.title: China’s used smartphone trade expands to South Asia and Africa
results.content: As the world's largest smartphone producer, China discards over 400 million devices annually and they are being snapped up by buyers from Africa and South Asia.

results.title: Around 700,000 displaced by volatile conflict in southern Ethiopia
results.content: NGO Islamic Relief says fighting between ethnic groups competing for land and wealth has seen widespread destruction of homes and disruption of services.

results.title: Germany: Berlin student protest targets rearmament and compulsory service
results.content: Thousands of students marched through Berlin, on Friday 20 November 2026, protesting against the country's rapid military rearmament and fears of a return to compulsory military service. Their protest formed part of a wider wave of youth demonstrations across Europe.

results.title: UN, Senegal urge regional action to stop migrant traffickers
results.content: The United Nations' migration agency and Senegal on Friday called for action against migrant trafficking networks, amid a resurgence of people trying to reach Europe by boat.

results.content: Scores of Palestinian children gathered on Friday along Gaza's Mediterranean coast in Khan Younis, exercising on the sand before heading into the water for swimming lessons.

results.title: Turkey: Activists chant 'shame' as COP31 negotiations falter
results.content: Climate activists denounced the proposed outcome of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday 20 November 2026, accusing governments of failing to deliver meaningful progress on tackling climate change. They chanted "shame" as negotiations approached their deadline.

results.title: Italy: Workers and students stage nationwide strike over living costs
results.content: Workers and students marched through Rome, on Friday 20 November 2026, joining a nationwide strike over stagnant wages, rising living costs and government spending priorities. Protesters also demanded more funding for education and criticised military spending.

results.title: Lebanese journalist injured in Israeli strike receives CPJ Press Freedom Award
results.content: AFP journalist Christina Assi, who lost a leg in an Israeli strike reporting from the Lebanese border and has become a vocal campaigner for reporters' safety, is honoured by the Committee to Protect Journalists.

results.title: Ukraine: Rescue teams search wreckage after deadly Russian strike on Kyiv
results.content: A Russian overnight attack on Kyiv, Ukraine, killed eight people on Friday 20 November 2026, according to Associated Press, leaving buildings and warehouses damaged across the capital. Firefighters battled blazes as emergency crews searched the wreckage and police collected evidence.

results.title: South Africa's murder rate falls but killings average 60 a day
results.content: South Africa recorded fewer murders between July and September with 5,590 people killed, continuing a downward trend in violent crime, the police ministry said on Friday. The country's murder rate still averages 60 a day.

results.title: Myanmar rejects ICJ Rohingya genocide ruling as 'unfair'
results.content: Myanmar's government on Thursday rejected an International Court of Justice ruling holding the country responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, calling the decision unfair.

results.title: Activists protest failure of COP31 to advance on moving away from fossil fuels
results.content: Civil society groups and activists on Friday protested against UN climate talks' failure to advance ideas to move away from fossils fuels.

results.title: Tunisian rights activist Sihem Bensedrine sentenced to 5 years in prison
results.content: Tunisian rights activist Sihem Bensedrine has been sentenced to five years in prison by the country’s criminal chamber for financial corruption.
